info: Handheld or table-mounted saw used for making fast, straight cuts in wood.
Used to shave thin layers of wood off a board to flatten and smooth it.
A handheld tool with a sharp beveled edge used for carving, paring, and cleaning out joints.
A thicker, heavier chisel designed to be struck with a mallet to chop deep rectangular holes (mortises).
Specialized power tool for making accurate crosscuts and miter joints at specific angles.
A woodworking tool consisting of a circular saw blade, mounted on an arbor, that is driven by an electric motor.
A power tool used to rout out (hollow out) an area, create decorative edges, or cut profiles in wood.
A slider-operating clamp used to hold wood pieces tightly together during gluing or assembly.
A wooden-headed hammer used to strike chisels or assemble wood joints without marring the timber.
A traditional tool used to scribe a line parallel to a reference edge or surface for precise joinery.
A handsaw that cuts on the pull stroke, allowing for a thinner blade and cleaner, more precise cuts.
A saw with a thin, flexible blade tensioned in a C-shaped steel frame, used for cutting intricate external shapes and interior cutouts.
A woodworking rule with an interchangeable head used for laying out 45-degree and 90-degree angles and measuring depths.
A small, handheld plane designed to cut end-grain and clean up sharp edges or small high spots.
A flat piece of steel used to scrape away microscopic shavings of wood to achieve a glass-smooth finish.
